title: Arson and crude bomb blasts reported in 11 districts; 29 arrested
excerpt: Police blame activists of the banned Awami League and Chhatra League. Field teams in Dhaka, Gopalganj, Shariatpur and Faridpur face the most disruption.

image.alt: The road deck of the Padma Bridge, on the Dhaka-Bhanga route, under a cloudy sky

content:
Twenty-two vehicles were set on fire in 11 districts and crude bombs exploded in at least 28 places in the 24 hours to Tuesday morning, 10 November, Prothom Alo reported, citing police. No deaths were reported. Several people, including police officers, were injured in clashes in Tungipara, Gopalganj.

Where it happened

  • Vehicle fires: four in Dhaka city, three in Chattogram city and 15 in Narayanganj, Naogaon, Gazipur, Patuakhali, Mymensingh, Gaibandha, Satkhira, Bogura, Manikganj, South Keraniganj and Faridpur.
  • Crude bombs: 19 locations in Dhaka, according to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, including eight or nine blasts at Dhaka University on Sunday evening. Others were in Manikganj, Gopalganj, Chattogram, Shariatpur, Cox’s Bazar and Rangpur.
  • Padma Bridge: between about 1:30am and 2:30am on Tuesday, a crowd blocked the Dhaka-Bhanga Expressway at the Zajira end of the bridge, set off crude bombs and damaged two trucks, Prothom Alo reported. Traffic stopped for nearly an hour.

Who police blame

Police sources blame leaders and activists of the banned Awami League and its student wing, Chhatra League, and link the violence to Sheikh Hasina’s announcement that she would return to Bangladesh. These are police claims and have not been independently verified. The banned Chhatra League had announced a nationwide blockade for 10 November on Facebook, according to the newspaper.

Police headquarters reported 29 arrests from Saturday to Monday, and the Dhaka Metropolitan Police at least 33 in connection with incidents in Dhaka. Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir told superintendents in all 64 districts to step up patrols and intelligence work and to make targeted arrests rather than mass arrests. Extra police were sent to Gopalganj, Shariatpur, Madaripur and Faridpur.

Why it matters

Several of the affected districts host NGO field programmes, and the Dhaka-Bhanga Expressway is the main road link to the southwest. Organisations with staff travelling by road, especially at night and through Gopalganj, Shariatpur, Madaripur and Faridpur, may want to review movement plans and check-in procedures until the situation settles.

What to watch

  • Whether further blockades are announced and how widely they are observed.
  • Whether police keep to targeted arrests, as the IGP instructed.
